inconsistencies: #36928 (31.x) and #36929 (30.x) backport the identical fix (#36927) to different maintenance branches; review them together, 31.x first. #36589 is the same family of maintenance-branch build backports for 32.x.
Chain: #36844 (iwyu base, five core files) must merge before #36808 (iwyu in fuzz tests), which is explicitly based on it. #36844 was banded below the PR it unblocks; raised to match.

Chain: #36082 (Guix builds in CI) is described as the infrastructure needed to introduce fully static Linux builds in #25573; review #36082 first even though #25573 carries the larger user-facing benefit.
Chain: #36781 (clang-tidy param naming) is based on #36743 (-Wmissing-declarations/prototypes), which itself depends on #36813; #36743 first.

Overlapping compiler-baseline work: #36042 (GCC 13 minimum) and #36033 (C++23 requirement) address the same transition at different depths. #36042 is the incremental step and should be decided first; if #36033 is accepted it subsumes it.

The warning-flag family (#35911 -Wmissing-noreturn, #36167 -Wunused, #36268 -Wextra-semi, #36743 -Wmissing-prototypes) all enable a new -W flag plus large mechanical churn across 65-177 files; they will conflict with each other and should be sequenced rather than reviewed in parallel.
Multiprocess build chain: #35068 (depends CMake package discovery) fixes native_libmultiprocess build failures and should be reviewed before the other multiprocess build PRs (#35454, #32387, #19460).
result.notes: Only one band change (#36844 P4 to P3, to sit above the PR it unblocks). The ordering departs from the by-score order mainly in one systematic way: the category ranks release integrity and actual platform/CI breakage above contributor-convenience tooling and internal hygiene, so concrete failure fixes (#36928/#36929, #36872, #36587, #36838, #36709, #36839) were lifted above feature/cleanup PRs that had scored higher (#33145, #28690, #34721, #35197, #35911, #36167). #36534 (hardening flags lost from release binaries) and #36589 (broken release builds) are the strongest P1 candidates after #35765 if the band needs widening.
